text:
ashley: @jordan @mike_s quick heads-up — found a debug dump in a staging pod that includes an auth header and a user email. filing here to scope impact and get comms/legal input. snippet below (redacted).

ashley: ```
2026-03-17T14:02:11Z INFO RequestHandler handleRequest user_email="user@example.com" Authorization="Bearer stg-abc123********"
```

ashley: path is /var/log/app/debug.log. I grepped s3://redwood-staging-backups and found 3 matching objects. PR to remove debug logging: https://git.redwood/infr/containers/pulls/12

jordan: ack. can you confirm exact s3 keys and rough number of affected files? did this get rsynced to long-term backups? :eyes:

ashley: keys: staging/2026-03-17/debug.log, staging/2026-03-15/debug.log, staging/2026-02-27/debug.log. rough count looks like 3 files, each ~12MB. at least some were included in daily backups.

mike_s: staging only? if s3 has them we should rm the objects and rotate any tokens that might be live. do we know if tokens are real or placeholder?

ashley: token looks like active staging tokens (matched prefix). i'm expiring matching staging tokens now: `scripts/expire_tokens.sh --env=staging --pattern="stg-abc123*"`

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2034 — Sev2 — scope: staging logs & S3 backups — assignees: @mike_s, @ashley

incident-bot: PagerDuty notified for eng-oncall.

jordan: recommended immediate steps:
1) remove S3 objects: `aws s3 rm s3://redwood-staging-backups/staging/2026-03-17/debug.log` (and the other two)
2) run redact job: `redact-backups --prefix=staging --pattern=debug.log`
3) rotate any referenced service/staging tokens

tara-legal: quick guidance: staging still counts as customer data for privacy. if any `user_email` fields contain customer addresses we need to loop in privacy for notification assessment. internal-only comms OK for now; do not send external comms until we have counts & impact. collect affected user count and whether data persisted beyond backups.

ashley: initial sweep finds ~12 unique emails across the three files — mostly internal test accounts, but 2 appear to be actual customer emails. i'll compile an exact list and scrub IDs before sharing with legal.

mike_s: i'll delete the S3 objects now and kick off the redaction job. ETA ~12m. after deletion i'll post confirmation and a short internal comms draft.

ashley: draft internal comms for legal review: "We discovered debug logs in staging containing two customer email addresses and one staging auth token. We removed backups and rotated tokens. No production exposure detected. We're continuing investigation." @tara-legal PTAL.

tara-legal: internal comms approved. external comms: hold until we confirm which customers were impacted and any contractual obligations. if confirmed that customer data was present in backups, privacy team will assess notification requirements; i'll coordinate. :white_check_mark:

jordan: one more ops ask — add a guard in helm values to prevent containers from starting with `--debug` and default log.level: INFO. i'll open a quick PR for the chart change.

ashley: related PRs: stop-debug PR https://git.redwood/services/logging/pulls/78 and helm change https://git.redwood/charts/core/pulls/9

mike_s: deletion done — `aws s3 rm` complete for the three keys. redact job started: job id redact-20260317-09. posting incident updates to INC-2034.

ops-bot: INC-2034 status updated: containment in progress.

ashley: thanks all. tagging this thread resolved for comms until legal asks for more. ping me for follow-ups. :pray:
